clue.text: Noted in legend to be excellent

definitions.meaning: celebrated in fable or myth, the word's original sense

explanation.definitionFit: The word first meant told of in fables, and in casual speech it means terrific.

clue.text: Women and conjurors use it

explanation.surface: Ladies and magicians share some tool or trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's stick is the classic prop waved by a stage illusionist.

clue.text: Battle I found in west London

indicators.note: the letter I is said to be found in the place, so it goes inside it

parts.note: Acton is a district of west London

explanation.surface: Someone discovered a battle taking place in west London.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district in west London; 'found in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight between armed forces is an engagement, a military sense of the word.

clue.text: Pair of international diplomats divorce

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is the body of international diplomats
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Two diplomats from a world body get divorced.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or detach two linked things, as railway carriages are parted.

clue.text: Feeble piece of training for building insulation

parts.note: a damp squib is feeble, so damp means limp or ineffective
a course is a programme of training

explanation.surface: A weak training session for a construction job.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of waterproof material laid low in a wall stops rising moisture, a kind of building insulation.

clue.text: Rare fright, catching cold

indicators.note: the word for fright catches, or holds, the letter for cold inside it

parts.note: a fright is a scare
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An unusual fright that leaves someone with a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply is hard to find, a synonym.

clue.text: Caribbean fruit product — excellent tin

parts.note: jam is made from fruit
A1 means first-rate, written as AI
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A preserve from the West Indies, sold in a superb tin.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (top quality) is written AI in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from the island of Jamaica is from the Caribbean.

clue.text: Pick up weapon to obtain some gold

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word for weapon, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
to obtain is to get

explanation.surface: Someone collects a firearm in order to get hold of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' looks like a homophone signal but in this down answer it turns GUN upwards to give NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump of native gold found by a prospector is a small amount of the metal.

clue.text: Religious outside a church in shade

indicators.note: the word for a religious woman goes outside the letter A

parts.note: a nun is a religious, a member of an order
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun stands outside a church in the shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' is a noun here, a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle shade of meaning or colour is a slight difference.

clue.text: Thickened milk said to be for middle easterner

indicators.note: said signals that the word spoken out loud gives the answer's sound

parts.note: curd is milk thickened by souring

explanation.surface: Curdled milk is offered to someone from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a people from the region spanning Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

clue.text: Actor so well employed not taking offence

definitions.meaning: a performer given a fine role is cast in a fine role

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting a remark good-humouredly; read literally it describes a performer with a fine role.

clue.text: Ache, working as fielder

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: Someone aches while working as a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: LONG ON is a fielding position in cricket, deep on the leg side behind the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket position name used for the player stationed there.

clue.text: Saucy to prepare for a privileged ride here?

parts.note: gravy is a sauce, so saucy points to it
to train is to prepare

explanation.surface: Getting cheeky to prepare for a ride on a luxury service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests cheekiness but here leads to gravy, a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a cushy, well-paid position, pictured as an easy journey.

clue.text: He'll have a job to keep you busy

definitions.text: He'll have a job to keep you busy

parts.words: He'll have a job to keep you busy
parts.note: reads like someone struggling to keep you occupied, but describes one who gives you a job

explanation.definitionFit: The boss who hires you provides work that keeps you occupied.

clue.text: Babywear on son, so fashionable a dresser

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the babywear follows the son

parts.note: a nappy is worn by a baby (British for diaper)

explanation.surface: A baby's diaper on a son makes him such a sharp dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPPY is British for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A snappy dresser is stylish and smart, so the word means chic.

clue.text: Advanced, preparing to drop me

indicators.note: preparing these words means making them up into something new

explanation.surface: Someone moved up, preparing to drop me from the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised in rank, moved forward, a synonym.

clue.text: Red cards for footballers

definitions.meaning: one of the two red suits in a pack
Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club

explanation.walkthrough: Heart of Midlothian, known as Hearts, is a Scottish football club in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit of playing cards printed in red; also the nickname of a Scottish club.

clue.text: Protected in Leeds, hid in disguise

indicators.note: the letters of these words are put into a disguise, changed in order

explanation.surface: Someone was kept safe in Leeds, hiding in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarded or screened from harm, a synonym.

clue.text: Repressed writer put back

parts.note: a pen writes

indicators.note: back means the word put is read backwards

explanation.surface: An inhibited author is put back in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings held in and not expressed are bottled up, a synonym.

clue.text: About to put down extra weapon

parts.note: C is circa, about
to lay is to put down
more means extra

explanation.surface: Advice to set down an additional weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish broadsword is a weapon.

clue.text: Learning about a hot city

indicators.note: the word for learning goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: lore is traditional learning

explanation.surface: Study about a hot city.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city of Pakistan, an example.

clue.text: In the pictures, judge put at the front

indicators.note: the word for judge is placed in the word for the pictures

parts.note: pix is slang for pictures, films
a ref, or referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: At the cinema, a judge is placed in the front row.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach something at the beginning, as a syllable before a word.

clue.text: Obvious safeguard for inventor

definitions.meaning: the legal right protecting an invention

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means plainly evident; as a noun it is the exclusive right granted for an invention.

clue.text: Central heating control is matter host worried about

indicators.note: matter and host are worried about, shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Heating control matters, and the host is anxious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that regulates temperature automatically switches a heating system.

clue.text: Not initially friendly colleague

indicators.note: the word for friendly loses its first letter

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly

explanation.surface: A colleague who is not friendly at first.
explanation.walkthrough: PALLY loses its first letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or associate on the same side, a synonym.

clue.text: Drivers circling about zone

indicators.note: the letters for drivers go round the word for about

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British motorists' organisation
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Motorists go round and round a district.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a motoring breakdown club.
explanation.definitionFit: A region or district, a synonym.

clue.text: Force to accept a commendation

indicators.note: the word for force takes in, accepts, the letter A

parts.note: to prise is to force open

explanation.surface: Someone is made to accept a commendation.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressed approval or admiration, a synonym.

clue.text: Seeing helpers without arms holding the bridge

definitions.text: Seeing helpers without arms holding the bridge

parts.words: Seeing helpers without arms holding the bridge
parts.note: sounds like disarmed soldiers holding a crossing, but describes spectacles with no side pieces that clip onto the nose

explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned spectacles that grip the top of the nose instead of resting on the ears.
